summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -3 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates −; dollar −; brl 0; mxn −; risk 0; energy +; china −; breadth 0. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Coffee +14.6%; weakest: KC wheat -15.2%.

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 5.13% (+17 bp in a month), 2-year 4.81% (+5 bp); 2s10s curve +32 bp (+12 bp in a month). Rising long yields raise carry and funding costs and pull money out of commodities. A steepening curve led by the long end often reflects inflation or term-premium worries; T-bill yield 4.06% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.69 (+1.3% in a month, +3.5% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.024 (-1.7% in a month): little changed. USD/CNY 6.675 (-0.3%); USD/MXN 18.70 (+8.6%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -0.1% in a month (+13.3% YTD); VIX 16.7. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 97.88 $/bbl (+9.8% in a month), Brent 109.88, ULSD 4.606 $/gal (+2.7%), natural gas 2.78 (-7.2%). Higher crude lifts biofuel margins (soybean oil, corn for ethanol) and synthetic-fibre costs (supports cotton), but raises diesel, drying and freight costs.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -2.9% in a month, Shanghai Composite -6.0%, Hang Seng -5.6%, yuan +0.3% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 15 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (45%); S&P GSCI +0.7% in a month; gold -5.2%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
